To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The properties of e–e + plasma produced by a laser pulse are determined by the laser pulse parameters, in particular the field strength and the spectrum of the pulse, and by the time of the interaction.
the properties of the EPPP created by a single pulse of a laser field are determined by the field strength, its form, and its spectrum.
the properties of e–e+pairs created in vacuum by the laser pulses are sensitive to the laser field form, spectrum, and pulse duration, as well as to the pulse intensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the dynamical Schwiger effect in the multiphotonic domain.
the investigation of the influence of a laser field on the properties of e–e + plasmas created from the vacuum in the multiphotonic domain (γ > 1).
the influence of the laser pulse parameters on the properties of the e–e+ plasma created from vacuum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the laser pulse parameters have significant effects on the properties of the e–e+ plasma created from vacuum.
the influence of pulse parameters on the properties of the created e–e+ plasma is significant and should be taken into account in the interpretation of the experiments.
the laser field parameters, the pulse duration, and the laser intensity, as well as the pulse shape, are of great importance for the properties of the e–e+ plasmas created from vacuum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we investigated the influence of the laser pulse parameters on the properties of the electron-positron pair plasma created from a vacuum.
we have investigated the dependence of the properties of an electron-positron pair plasmas on the form of the external laser pulse.
the EPPP distribution function depends significantly on both the pulse shape and spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EPPP distribution function depends strongly on the field strength (the multiphoton domain) and the pulse shape (the adiabaticity parameter), but not the field spectrum.
the distribution of the created e–e+ pairs is strongly dependent on the form of the laser field and the parameters of the laser pulse.

the EPPP distribution function can be calculated for any arbitrary laser pulse, which is important because in the laboratory one usually deals with pulses of a complex structure, which cannot be represented by a single harmonic.
